source.author: verg
source.text: cesserit Ausonio si fors victoria Turno, convenit Evandri victos discedere ad urbem, cedet Iulus agris, nec post arma ulla rebelles Aeneadae referent ferrove haec regna lacessent, sin nostrum adnuerit nobis Victoria Martem ut potius reor et potius di numine firment, non ego nec Teucris Italos parere iubebo nec mihi regna peto: paribus se legibus ambae invictae gentes aeterna in foedera mittant.
source.text_original: cesserit Ausonio si fors victoria Turno, / convenit Evandri victos discedere ad urbem, / cedet Iulus agris, nec post arma ulla rebelles / Aeneadae referent ferrove haec regna lacessent, / sin nostrum adnuerit nobis Victoria Martem / (ut potius reor et potius di numine firment), / non ego nec Teucris Italos parere iubebo / nec mihi regna peto: paribus se legibus ambae / invictae gentes aeterna in foedera mittant.
source.text_english: If chance should grant victory to Ausonian Turnus, it is agreed that the defeated must depart to Evander’s city, Iulus will yield the fields, and after this the rebellious Aeneadae shall not again take up arms or challenge these kingdoms with the sword; but if Victory shall nod assent to our Mars—as I rather think, and may the gods rather confirm it by their will—then I will not command the Italians to obey the Teucrians, nor do I seek kingdoms for myself: let both unconquered peoples enter into an eternal treaty on equal laws.

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: hanc mihi militiam, veterum quae pulchrior actis, adnue daque animum.
reuse.text_original: 'hanc mihi militiam, veterum quae pulchrior actis, / adnue daque animum.
reuse.text_english: Grant me this service, more splendid than the deeds of old, and give me courage.
